Topic: The Magic of Dandelin Spheres: Unveiling Conic Sections

Target audience: High school or undergraduate geometry students

Section: section_1 — Introduction: The Geometry of a Sliced Cone

Lecture lines:
Slice a cone to reveal conic sections.
Circles, ellipses, parabolas, and hyperbolas emerge.
Dandelin Spheres explain these shapes perfectly.
Visualize the flashlight beam on the wall.
Discover the hidden geometric Rosetta Stone.

Planned animations:
Fade in a 3D representation of a cone (light color: #FFFFFF).
Introduce a plane intersecting the cone at an angle.
Highlight the resulting elliptical cross-section with color #FF5733.
Rotate the scene to visualize the cone's depth.
Add labels 'Cone' and 'Ellipse' in #E0E0E0 color.

Section: section_2 — Prerequisite Concept: Tangency and Focus

Lecture lines:
A sphere meets a plane at one point.
Tangents from a point to spheres are equal.
This property is our essential key.

Planned animations:
Display a circle and a line tangent to it in #FFD700.
Animate a point moving along the line to demonstrate tangency.
Highlight the focus point with a pulse animation in #32CD32.

Section: section_3 — The Dandelin Construction

Lecture lines:
Place a sphere inside the cone.
The sphere touches the cone's inner circle.
The sphere also touches the slicing plane.
The contact point is the conic focus.
This creates the elegant Dandelin construction.

Planned animations:
Introduce a Dandelin sphere tangent to the cone and plane.
Label the contact points 'F1' and 'F2' using color #87CEEB.
Animate the spheres shrinking towards the focus points.
Show the intersection of the plane with the cone's surface.
Highlight the focal property relationship using color #FF4500.

Section: section_4 — Proving the Ellipse Property

Lecture lines:
Point P sits on our ellipse.
Distances to two foci add up.
Sum remains constant for every point.
Tangent properties prove this sum invariant.
Dandelin Spheres confirm the ellipse property.

Planned animations:
Display two paths from a point on the ellipse to foci.
Animate the sum of distances 'd1 + d2' remaining constant.
Flash the ellipse boundary in #FFA500 to show consistency.

Section: section_5 — Conclusion and Real-world Application

Lecture lines:
Geometry links 3D solids to 2D curves.
Satellite dishes and orbits use these forms.
Conic sections define our physical world.

Planned animations:
Display a real-world elliptical architectural arch.
Overlay the elliptical geometry onto the structure in #00FFFF.
Zoom out to reveal the cone-slice origin of the shape.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject
